CLINICAL INSIGHT
Urinary Tract Infections and Cranberry Juice
Urinary tract infections (UTIs) are much more common in women than 
men because of the shorter female urethra. Elderly women have the 
highest incidence of UTI, and it is thought to be related to the loss of 
estrogen after menopause. Patients who are catheterized are also at 
high risk. The bacteria most commonly involved are E. coli resulting 
from the close proximity of the anus to a woman’s urethra. Treatment 
is usually antibiotics to resolve the infection and phenazopyridine is 
used as an anesthetic to decrease symptoms. It temporarily changes 
the color of a woman’s urine to bright orange or red. It is contraindi-
cated in renal failure.
Nutritionally, tannins or proanthocyanidins in cranberry juice and blue-
berry juice may inhibit the adherence of E. coli bacteria to the epithelial 
cells. Coffee, alcohol, and sodas should be avoided because they irritate 
the urinary tract and cause dehydration. In normal kidney function drink-
ing 6 to 8 ounces of water daily is recommended.
